  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],

  "descriptive_findings": [

    "Overall success rate across all paradigms was 73.0% (SD=0.44), with mean Time-to-Target of 2.81 seconds (SD=2.08).",
    "Path Efficiency averaged 0.47 (SD=0.47) with extreme right skew (max=29.82), suggesting occasional highly inefficient trajectories.",
    "Average Speed was 12.50 units/s (SD=4.46), while Angular Dispersion (AD) averaged 0.38 (SD=0.24), indicating moderate directional variability in heading.",
    "Eight mice contributed data, with SC21LM contributing the most trials (10,986) and SC11LM the fewest (7,233), suggesting relatively balanced mouse-level representation."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Sample size imbalance is extreme: Combined has 14.7× more trials than Bright Visual Only, limiting statistical precision for rare paradigms.",
    "Success rate variability (binary outcome) shows high dispersion (SD=0.44), but paradigm-specific rates cannot be determined from marginal statistics alone.",
    "Path Efficiency shows massive variability (SD nearly equals mean, CV≈98%) with extreme outliers, potentially masking paradigm effects.",
    "Time-to-Target ranges from 0.5s to 201.4s, indicating highly heterogeneous task difficulty or behavioral strategies across paradigms.",
    "Sham and Bright Visual Only have the smallest sample sizes (3,505 and 3,323 trials), making comparisons involving these groups most uncertain."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "The Combined stimulation paradigm dominates the dataset, reflecting its likely status as the primary experimental condition of interest. The dramatic underrepresentation of Sham and Bright Visual Only (each <5% of data) severely limits confident inference about these conditions. The high overall success rate (~73%) suggests the task was achievable but not trivial. Path Efficiency's extreme outliers indicate some trials involved highly circuitous paths—possibly exploratory behavior or disorientation—whose distribution may differ by paradigm. Without paradigm-specific means, we cannot determine whether Combined stimulation improves metrics like Path Efficiency or reduces Time-to-Target versus unimodal or sham conditions, which would be the key translational question for neuroprosthetic or sensory feedback applications.",
  "limitations": [
    "Only marginal (dataset-level) statistics are available; no paradigm-specific means, standard deviations, or distributions are provided, preventing direct group comparisons.",
    "Extreme sample size imbalance across paradigms (range: 3,323 to 48,846 trials) creates highly uneven statistical power.",
    "Path Efficiency contains extreme outliers (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47) suggesting non-normal distributions that may require transformation or robust methods.",
    "No information on mouse-by-paradigm random effects or repeated measures structure; treating trials as independent would inflate Type I error.",
    "Temperature=0.75 and Kimi model with basic prompt template are experimental parameters whose effects on data quality are unknown.",
    "AD is labeled as 'angular dispersion' but its exact computational definition and units (0-1 bounded) are not specified in the artifacts."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Compute paradigm-specific descriptive statistics (mean, SD, median, IQR) and success rates for all five variables, followed by mixed-effects models with Mouse as random effect to account for repeated measures. Prioritize pairwise comparisons of Combined versus each unimodal and Sham condition using appropriate multiple comparison corrections. Visualize distributions (especially Path Efficiency) to assess normality assumptions and consider robust regression or rank-based methods given the observed outliers. Power analysis or Bayesian credible intervals would help quantify uncertainty for the underrepresented Sham and Bright Visual Only paradigms."
}
